finding.claim: The /checkout handler computes the charge total from client-supplied price and qty. It never looks up prices in the catalog and never validates qty. An authenticated user can set price to 0.01 or qty to a negative number and pay an arbitrary, even zero or negative, amount. Sibling route /checkout-v2 (lines 10-18) looks up the price server-side and clamps qty, so v1 is the unprotected sibling.
finding.sink: req.payments.charge(req.user.id, total) at cart.js:6, and the response at cart.js:7

trace.note: POST /checkout entry; no validation middleware is visible in this file
total = sum(i.price * i.qty) taken directly from the request body
charge is called with the attacker-derived total

finding.guards_checked: No server-side price lookup, no qty bounds or integer check, no check that price is positive, no total sanity check. The only guard is the implied authentication behind req.user, which does not constrain the amounts. The v2 route's catalog.price lookup and Math.max(1, Math.floor(qty)) are absent here. Only cart.js exists, so any upstream middleware is not visible.

verdict.guard_found: none (only implied authentication via req.user; no validation, no price lookup, no qty bounds in cart.js)
verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty and cart.js:6 passes it to req.payments.charge with no price lookup or qty/positivity check, unlike /checkout-v2 at cart.js:13-14; the only caveat is that upstream middleware outside cart.js can't be seen, since cart.js is the only file.
